1.explanation:
• Accordion/README.md — shows how users consume the Accordion and any documented props.  
• Accordion/index.js — the entry point that wires up prop definitions and exports the component.  
• Accordion/Accordion.js — contains the core Accordion logic where you’d introduce the new `align` prop and default.  
• AccordionItem/index.js — exports the individual item component so you can pass the `align` prop down.  
• AccordionItem/AccordionItem.js — renders the chevron icon and heading; this is where conditional placement based on `align` must occur.  
• Accordion/_accordion.scss — holds the CSS rules that position the chevron. You’ll need to add modifiers for `start` vs. `end` alignment to get the correct layout.
1.bug_scenario: The bug scenario centers around adding a new `align` prop to the Carbon Accordion so that its chevron (expand/collapse icon) can appear at either the start or the end of the heading. In the provided screenshot, the custom wrapper defaults to `align="start"`, placing the chevron to the left of the heading text on a dark background. Carbon’s upstream Accordion currently always aligns the chevron at the end (right) of the heading. To reproduce and verify this behavior, you’ll need to inspect both the Accordion parent component (where props are defined and passed) and the AccordionItem (where the chevron is rendered and styled), plus any related style definitions that position that icon.
